 Share 26m ago 07.32 EDT Tom Garry at Goodison Park 
 There’s a thick layer of low-hanging cloud over Goodison Park that is providing a fairly bland, gloomy and wintery feel ahead of this lunchtime WSL clash, but both teams arrive here in positive moods after good midweek victories in the League Cup.
 The splash of purple – used by the hosts to redecorate some of this famous old ground’s exterior – offers a bit of colour amid the grey scenes, but otherwise the surroundings are familiar for veteran Everton fans. I’ve just spoken to a few home supporters who say they enjoy coming here for the nostalgia. They would also love a win, which would propel them up to fourth in the table.

 Share 43m ago 07.16 EDT Bruno Fernandes starts for Manchester United against Chelsea
 Bruno Fernandes has been named in Michael Carrick’s starting lineup to face Chelsea this lunchtime and will wear the armband. Fernandes held clear-the-air talks with Carrick this week after he was dropped to the bench for the defeat to Bournemouth last Sunday following comments about the manager’s tactics in the loss to Como.
 View image in fullscreen United arrive at the Bridge. Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty Images Share 53m ago 07.06 EDT Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane returns to action today in Der Klassiker, which is a 5.30pm (GMT) kick-off at the Allianz Arena. His record against Borussia Dortmund is, well, quite good – six goals in six Bundesliga games. But you’d expect nothing less, to be honest.
 “Kane was a top player in England already,” Dortmund manager Niko Kovac said this week, “but to make another step up at his age that’s sensational and shows the danger and the quality of a player like that. We won’t get this done one on one, we’ll need to do it together.”
 Kane was given a guard of honour by his teammates before Wednesday’s DFB Pokal game against Magdeburg, which he sat out on the bench.
 View image in fullscreen Harry Kane gets a guard of honour. Photograph: Midori Ikenouchi/Hasan Bratic/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock Kane’s compatriot Aaron Danks will take charge of Bayern Munich for the second weekend in a row with Vincent Kompany still absent. Bayern said on Wednesday that Kompany had been discharged from hospital after he was admitted last week after collapsing in training. Kompany is continuing to recover at home after a meningeal infection.
 “No big changes, no big differences for us. We will be ready and super competitive,” Danks said of Bayern’s approach to Der Klassiker. “There is a difference (in coaching). Vinnie did not want his assistant coaches to be mini-Vinnies. We ‌are all different but we complement each other.”

 Since then, the two sides have taken diverging paths – Coventry spent another season in the second tier while Sunderland’s post-promotion form led them all the way into Europe. But today they meet as near-equals – they occupy the bottom two places in the Premier League table.

Illustration: Nathan Daniels/The Guardian Share 2h ago 06.13 EDT Manchester United Women are on a roll right now. After some teething problems under new manager Eva Olid, United have won seven of their last eight games in all competitions and drew with the WSL champions in the Manchester derby last weekend.
 Speaking after United’s 3-0 win over Burnley in the League Cup on Wednesday, Olid said: “This match is really good for momentum but we cannot relax on Saturday, we have Everton in the league. In the league, anything can happen and everyone is difficult to play.”
 Captain Maya Le Tissier had played every minute of United’s last 118 games until she was subbed against Burnley. “She knew [about the sub], because the records are good but I need to protect her,” Olid said. “I think she needed a rest and I think it was the best decision, but still, she’s starting all games.”
 Today’s game is, of course, taking place at Goodison Park, which Everton Women have to themselves after the men moved to Hill Dickinson Stadium.

Estêvão was left on the bench for the Carabao Cup game against Liverpool and has played just 47 minutes in the Premier League so far this season.

But everyone has to be ready because in any game they could be important. Este, his training and his attitude has been good.

 Bewildered1 31 October 2026 9:18am Here is the article in question and a snippet of Andy’s stat action …
 double quotation mark Mac Allister’s sense of responsibility extends to implementing Iraola’s instructions for his new team. Figures from Opta show the midfielder is winning more tackles per Premier League game this season – 2.3 on average compared to 1.8 last season; winning more duels (4.8 from 3.8); winning more aerial duels (0.9 from 0.6) and winning more possession (5.6 on average compared to 3.8).
 He is sacrificing the offensive side of his game to bring more aggression and organisation to the defensive aspect, and his touches in the opposition box, chances created, goals and assists are all down on last season as a consequence. Not that Iraola is complaining.

 Inter and Milan this week unveiled plans for their new stadium that will replace San Siro from the 2031-32 season, in time for Italy to co-host Euro 2032.
 The stadium, sponsored by Generali – Italy’s largest insurance company – will have a capacity of 71,500 seats and is expected to cost the two clubs €1.2bn (£1bn). The plans were revealed at a gala event at Milan’s Castello Sforzesco on Thursday – but some fans in attendance voiced their opposition to San Siro being demolished.
 Shortly before the briefing began, a group of Inter fans walked into the courtyard of the castle and unfurled a banner reading: “You will never extinguish the lights at San Siro,” and chanting: “Hands off San Siro.” Work on the new stadium is set to begin in 2028, on the site of the existing 75,000-capacity venue.

 Share 3h ago 05.09 EDT It is not all rosy at Chelsea either. A home defeat to Spurs can bring any season to a grinding halt and the manner of the performance last weekend has brought Xabi Alonso under scrutiny. Wednesday’s defeat to Liverpool in the Carabao Cup has not helped, with the domestic cups surely taking higher priority this season without European football.
 But perhaps the most concerning thing for Alonso is his growing injury list . In recent days and weeks he has lost Reece James, João Pedro and Maxence Lacroix – with none of them expected back for a few weeks at least. Emi Martínez could soon make a return from his broken jaw, but it will be Mike Penders in goal again today.
 Here are the predicted lineups for the lunchtime clash with Manchester United …
 View image in fullscreen Chelsea v Manchester United: probable starters in bold, contenders in italics Share 3h ago 05.00 EDT “It’s not always rosy and nice conversations,” Michael Carrick said on Thursday as he reflected on a difficult week at United amid speculation over his future and the general state of the club.
 United have gone eight games without a win after their worst league start in 40 years. They are 16th in the Premier League , one point above the relegation zone. Carrick suggested he had held talks with Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada this week …
 double quotation mark It’s pretty clear, it’s not always rosy and nice conversations between anyone, whether that’s between me and the players, whether that’s between me, Jason, Omar or the owners.
 It’s the truth, it’s the hard truth at times and it’s what we need to move forward. Whatever we need to move forward, we will do.
 On the reception he was given – and the boos his players received – at Old Trafford following defeat to Bournemouth last Sunday, Carrick said …
 double quotation mark I’ll be totally honest, it was mixed feelings for me. To have the appreciation from the supporters and that connection and that respect is something I feel strongly about.
 It wasn’t a nice situation but to feel that was important, of course, but it didn’t make me feel better in the fact that I’m with the players 100% and we’re all in it together. I’ve told the players that, I’m happy to say that.
 Carrick tells players ‘hard truth’ in attempt to turn Manchester United’s season around Read more View image in fullscreen Old Trafford was ‘mixed feelings’, says Michael Carrick. Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty Images Share Updated at  05.01 EDT 3h ago 04.54 EDT Manchester United: What’s gone on this week? Well, you would have got long odds on Michael Carrick being in the dugout at Stamford Bridge when he trudged down the tunnel at Old Trafford last weekend.
 Monday: The powers that be at Carrington – the immensely popular Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada – hold talks over Carrick’s future. Carrick attends an under-21s match at the training ground.
 Tuesday: Wilcox decides to give Carrick a chance to turn things around. Bruno Fernandes holds clear-the-air talks with Carrick after sitting out the defeat to Bournemouth. Eddie Howe emerges as United’s prime candidate if Carrick is sacked.
 Thursday: Carrick says he will not strip Fernandes of the captaincy and says he is not surprised to have kept his job as head coach. “Between us, we’ve got to make a difference and push things in a good direction,” Carrick says.
 Should Fernandes return to the United lineup at Chelsea today? If he does, he’ll lead them out as captain.
 Share 3h ago 04.44 EDT Suspicious bets for predicting Ballon d'Or under investigation
 A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police.
 It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award.
 Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outlet Upside’s investigation.
 Suspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigation Read more Share 3h ago 04.37 EDT Aston Villa to take legal action against Carragher for 'unacceptable insults'
 Aston Villa have announced plans to take legal action against Jamie Carragher following his “unacceptable insults” about the club and its supporters.
 Carragher told Villa fans to “shut the f*** up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job. Villa responded on Friday evening with a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris.
 “Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”

 Share 4h ago 04.25 EDT Preamble
 Hello and welcome to Matchday Live on a bumper day in the Premier League . I’ll be bringing you the latest news and buildup to eight top-flight games, with Chelsea v Manchester United on the menu at lunchtime. Michael Carrick lives to fight another day in the United dugout and so does Bruno Fernandes as captain after clear-the-air talks took place this week. We shall have to wait and see if Fernandes returns to the XI. Chelsea and Xabi Alonso could really do with a result after their poor display against Tottenham.
 Elsewhere, there are five 3pm kick-offs including Manchester City v Brighton ( again ) and the basement battle between Coventry (19th) and Sunderland (20th). Plus there is a first game in charge of Championship Burnley for Fabio Celestini for the visit of Portsmouth to Turf Moor. It really starts to get spooky after dark as Spurs host Crystal Palace and Aston Villa face Fulham .
 Two of British football’s grand old grounds host action as Everton take on Manchester United at Goodison in the WSL and Rangers face Aberdeen in the men’s Scottish League Cup semis at Hampden. Fleetwood , if anyone is asking, are at home to Bristol Rovers in League Two. Oh, and it’s Der Klassiker in Germany as Bayern Munich (and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane) host Borussia Dortmund. Is that everything? Nope, there’s a Milan derby , too.
 If you’re on your way to a game today or have anything to get off your chest, you can email me here . Comments will hopefully be open BTL shortly, too.
